column1: # The Stage 2 pair's undefended-branch ledger (#1408, parent #1401).
# Per function of bootstrap/stage2/compiler.c, how many of its branches
# nothing this repository runs ever takes -- once under each host compiler of
# the diverse pair. That set is where a divergence between compiler.kofun and
# its hand-maintained compiler.c transliteration can hide.
# A LISTED FUNCTION IS NOT WRONG. It is unwatched.
# AND A ROW IS NOT AUTOMATICALLY WORK. #1408 deliberately does not classify
# these as unreachable-by-construction versus reachable-but-uncovered --
# that judgement is per-region and belongs to the later children of #1401.
# This file is their work-list, so it has to say what a row does not mean.
# Some branches here cannot be reached by any fixture, because an earlier
# rule refuses first. The session working #1315 measured the shape: the
# `escaping store` and `escaping capture` reasons are unreachable, since
# Bytes is not an admitted record field type and cannot be captured, so
# E2S32 and E2S96 refuse before either is reached. They reported it rather
# than writing fixtures, because a fixture aimed there PASSES TODAY against
# a compiler that never implements the reason -- a defended-looking row
# defending nothing, which is worse than the undefended row it replaced.
# So: before writing a fixture to retire a row, check whether anything can
# reach it. A green fixture is not evidence that it could.
#   clang         clang version 22.1.8
#   basis         the union of the 158 driver rows and 1286 pinned *.kofun
#                 inputs that drivers.tsv and inputs.tsv held at that commit
#   totals        1925 untaken under gcc, 1836 under clang, across 360 functions
#   rows sha256   abf806f7516dc55b92405e1a90c17aa4c22d23b56612b0c4af1d09efd2500e9b   as measured, 360 rows
#                 a12bc80d63da0e97d520c321337fc733118d346cdc1519b8c4800733c1171f9a   as committed, 359 -- see below
# ONE MEASURED ROW HAS BEEN DELETED SINCE, AND THE TOTALS ABOVE STILL INCLUDE
# IT. #1548 renamed `bytes_parameter_discards` out of existence after this run
# (see the block below), so its row -- `4  4  bytes_parameter_discards` --
# names a function compiler.c no longer has. That is a stale record rather than
# an unwatched function, and mirror.tsv must carry a verdict per ledger row, so
# leaving it turns the staleness into a red gate. It is deleted here as it is
# on `main`, by the same reasoning and with the same arithmetic: the rows below
# sum to 1921 under gcc and 1832 under clang across 359 functions, and the
# difference from the measured totals is exactly that one row.
# THE BASIS COUNTS ABOVE ARE NOT THE COUNTS IN THIS TREE, and both differences
# are named rather than left to be discovered:
#   drivers  158 rows then, 157 now. Not a lost gate. #1582 replaced the two
#            leaf rows `bytes-carrier` and `bytes-mutation` with the
#            `bounded-bytes` aggregate that runs both, so the same two gates
#            execute under one name. Nothing was added or dropped.
#   inputs   1286 then, 1287 now -- see the next block.
# WHAT THIS MEASUREMENT DOES NOT COVER. #1548 landed after it, and it moved
# both halves of what a measurement is made of:
#   bootstrap/stage2/compiler.c                       +43 -11
#   tests/stage2/unused-function/unused_parameter.kofun    new, now pinned
# So no row below describes the discarded-parameter path, and the next
# measurement should expect the totals to RISE for a reason that is not a
# regression. The record on `main` before this one, taken at c005fc31, has
# exactly the same gap: #1548 landed after it too, and its header was not
# updated to say so. Naming the gap is the whole reason the `measured at`
# line exists, so it is named here for both.
# WHAT MOVED SINCE c005fc31. That record and this one measure a BYTE-IDENTICAL
# compiler.c -- verified, not assumed -- so every difference below is basis,
# not compiler. This basis is the earlier one plus three fixtures and nothing
# else, which makes the comparison one-directional by construction: coverage
# can only grow, so untaken can only fall.
#   totals   1963 -> 1925 under gcc,  1873 -> 1836 under clang
# Those four numbers compare the two MEASUREMENTS. The two committed files
# differ by one more row in each, because both have had the stale
# `bytes_parameter_discards` row deleted: 360 rows on `main` against 359 here.
# No function appears here that was absent there, which is what a superset
# basis requires. Seven rows fell and one left:
#   pattern_recovery_end   17 -> 3      match_arm_pattern_start   10 -> 9
#   pattern_match_open     13 -> 4      build_scope_hir_mode      28 -> 27
#   parse_pattern_atomic   27 -> 25     validate_move_assertions  19 -> 18
#   pattern_arm_arrow       9 -> 0      lower_body               141 -> 140
# READ THAT TABLE IN TWO PARTS, because only one part was predicted. #1508's
# classification found the untaken branches in the three recovery scanners
# reachable rather than refused by an earlier rule, and a scoped instrumented
# run predicted 34 gcc branches from the four functions on the left. The
# measurement moved exactly 34 there. The four on the right moved 4 more that
# nobody predicted: they are functions the new fixtures merely pass through on
# the way to the scanners. 34 + 4 = 38 = the drop in the gcc total, and the
# clang total closes the same way at 37. The prediction was good for the
# region it was about and silent about the rest, which is worth knowing before
# the next region is classified on the strength of one.
# AND ONE ROW LEFT THE FILE, which has never happened before. pattern_arm_arrow
# is fully covered and is gone from this ledger and from mirror.tsv. A row
# leaving is the event this file exists to make visible in the other direction
# -- the header below says an improvement nobody wrote down is slack for the
# next regression to hide in, so it is written down here with the prediction
# that matched it.
# COST, measured on this run rather than estimated -- it is the number the
# `verify`-or-not argument in tooling/gate-reachability/unreachable.tsv rests
# on, and the reason that file rather than the verify list is where this gate
# is accounted for:
#   gcc    drivers  5010s + corpus  809s =   97 min, drivers are 86% of it
#   clang  drivers  4860s + corpus  850s =   95 min, drivers are 85% of it
#   both   drivers  9870s + corpus 1659s =  192 min for the pair
#   8 cores. Load was read ONCE, by hand, at 11:07:53 as the run started:
#   2.33. No sampler ran for the following 192 minutes, so that figure
#   describes the start and nothing else. The run was scheduled against a
#   release freeze with two other sessions holding off the machine by
#   agreement, but an agreement is not a measurement and this file does not
#   record it as one.
# READ THE PHASE SPLIT, NOT THE ABSOLUTE. These wall-clock figures are
# observations from one shared-machine run, not a clean-machine cost or a
# controlled cross-host comparison. The reported phase shares describe only
# where each sequential host run spent its wall time; without a load sampler,
# no same-contention claim is made or inferred -- including against the 185
# minutes recorded at c005fc31, which this run's 192 cannot be compared to
# as a cost, only noted as having driven 3 more inputs.
# RETRIES. On each host `discovery` failed with exit=201 and was retried on
# attempts 1 through 3, matching the pinned driver-failures.tsv policy and
# the same behaviour recorded at c005fc31. Neither host recorded a corpus
# timeout.
# DETERMINISM (#1408 criterion 5). This basis has one fresh two-compiler
# measurement: the run recorded above. The 155-driver / 1258-input basis was
# measured twice at 6ee19d95 and d07bfcf5 and produced byte-identical rows,
# which is historical evidence for the harness rather than a repeat of this
# basis. A second run of this basis is still required before claiming
# byte-identical repeat determinism for it -- and because #1548 has already
# moved compiler.c underneath it, that repeat is no longer available: the
# next run measures a different compiler, and criterion 5 has to be met on
# the basis that exists then.
# Regenerate with:
#   sh tests/pair-coverage/check.sh --count
# Regeneration is deliberately manual: the number moving is the event this
# file exists to make visible. `sh tests/pair-coverage/check.sh` holds it
# exact in both directions -- more untaken than recorded is a regression,
# fewer is an improvement nobody wrote down.
